bullets.title: Fed rate-hike odds surge to ~56-60% for September after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech
bullets.body: Markets now price a 54-60% probability of a 25bp Fed hike at the September 16 FOMC meeting, up sharply from prior levels, with a second hike now at 68.5% odds for January. Warsh flagged end of 'secular stagnation,' a global investment surge reversing savings gluts, and signaled neutral rate may have risen, supporting higher term premium. August CPI on Sept 11 is the critical gating print before the decision.

bullets.title: 10Y Treasury yield hits 4.75%, 5Y at 4.5%—highest levels since January 2025
bullets.body: Iran conflict-driven oil surge and hawkish Warsh commentary triggered bear-steepening in Treasuries, pushing the 10-year to 4.75% and the 5-year to 4.5%, both the highest since January 2025. The 30-year yield is at a 19-year high. JPM flagged that the hawkish Jackson Hole reaction failed to lower long-end yields as the market expected, and Goldman's derivatives desk called this 'starting to look ungood.' FSB Chair Bailey separately warned G-20 of disorderly correction risk tied to sovereign debt fragilities.

bullets.title: JPMorgan shifts tactically cautious/neutral on US equities; September seasonality and momentum breakdown cited
bullets.body: JPM's trading desk moved to tactically cautious, citing: (i) probable September Fed hike if Warsh holds, (ii) choppy positioning for 3-4 weeks, (iii) post-Labor Day credit spread widening risk, (iv) September seasonality weakness, and (v) momentum factors down 21-34% from June highs vs. typical 10-15% drawdowns. Recommendation: reduce net-longs, favor Mag7 over AI/Memory/Semis, like Software and Large-Cap Banks, hedge with short credit ETFs and long VIX products until the Sept 16 meeting.

bullets.title: Middle East escalation drives WTI +2.8% to $85.91; Iran conflict and Hormuz tensions the primary macro driver
bullets.body: Iran fired at least eight ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in Jordan; Trump vowed retaliation; CENTCOM denied Iranian mine-strike claims in Hormuz. Brent crude is reportedly +88% YTD. Morgan Stanley raised 4Q WTI forecast to $96/bbl (from $76) and Brent to $100 (from $75). Treasury Secretary Bessent said oil prices 'will come down' once the Iran situation resolves and that Iranian oil on water is limited to ~30M barrels due to the blockade. Venezuela oil deal (Vance: 'significant production expected') could provide offset but impact is years away.

bullets.title: Bessent CNBC blitz: core inflation 'very tame,' traditional policy doesn't hike into supply shocks, growth is the only debt exit
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent argued core inflation remains very restrained, said 'traditionally you don't raise into a supply shock,' and maintained that the only way out of US debt is to grow the economy. He aligned himself with Warsh on bonds, said he has not bought anything in the bond market yet, declined to speculate on Fed actions, and expects BOJ actions to support yen appreciation. He also dismissed the Druckenmiller editorial, saying Druckenmiller 'lost money' the day he sent it.

bullets.title: Dallas Fed Manufacturing index surges to 11.6 vs. 1.6 estimate; new orders jump to +22.0
bullets.body: The August Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index printed 11.6 versus a 1.6 consensus estimate, with new orders at +22.0 (vs. +6.4 prior), production at +16.1, and shipments at +14.1. The word 'uncertainty' was flagged as the dominant theme in survey commentary despite the strong headline. ISM Manufacturing (tomorrow) expected at 55.0 vs. 55.2 survey.

bullets.title: August 2026 monthly recap: Nasdaq +3.93%, S&P +2.62%, led by NVDA +9.8%, TSLA +18.2%, MSFT +9.2%; software IGV +16.3%
bullets.body: August 2026 saw mega-cap tech dominate with NVDA posting blowout earnings and 70% revenue-growth guidance for FY28. Software sector was very strong (IGV +16.3%, up 4 of 5 months); SOX +2.0% after July slump. Market priced ~38bp of Fed hikes through year-end, highest in over a month. Laggards included airlines, utilities, A&D, and China tech.

bullets.title: Anthropic's valuation surge to $965B drove ~$150B in S&P 500 'other income,' inflating aggregate EPS 51% YoY
bullets.body: Anthropic's valuation jumped from $380B to $965B in Q2 2026, generating investment gains that flowed through 'other income' for GOOGL (~$98B gain) and AMZN (~$53B). This circular financing dynamic is the primary driver of S&P 500 headline earnings growth of 51% YoY—a measure most analysts exclude at the individual-company level. S&P 500 forward P/E fell from 25 to 21 this year, now at post-COVID average levels.

bullets.title: Goldman vol trader says risk-reward for owning upside 'extremely compelling' despite seasonal stress; October VIX call spreads recommended as hedge
bullets.body: A Goldman vol trader stated that despite seasonal market stress, the risk-reward for owning upside is extremely compelling. Separately, an analyst recommends October VIX call spread hedges given September averages 22% VIX gains over the past five years and net VIX short positioning is very elevated (implying the crowd is underhedged). The S&P 500 NDR cycle composite is entering its historically most challenging stretch of the year.

bullets.title: Macro managers rotating to hard assets and global equities vs. US stocks amid policy noise
bullets.body: Market sources note macro managers are rotating away from soft assets and US stocks toward hard assets and global equities as repeated rhetorical policy statements with limited follow-through fail to drive meaningful market movement. German DAX fell 1.09%, CAC 40 -0.6%; European bonds extended losses with Italian 10-year yields up 5bps to 4.15%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 utilities sector CPI divergence: sector down 5.2% in August despite S&P +2.62%; wildfire liability bill SB492 devastates PCG/EIX/SRE
bullets.body: California SB492 wildfire bill failed to shift subrogation risk from utilities. PCG fell 24% and EIX fell 26%; SRE also downgraded at Mizuho. Multiple brokers downgraded all three names. Goldman rates SRE Buy at $109 citing lower California exposure. Meanwhile, hyperscalers' non-commenced power leases reached 25.5 GW (+346% YoY), continuing to drive renewable and IPP growth.

bullets.title: NVIDIA invests $3.5B in MediaTek convertible bonds; NVLink Fusion ecosystem expansion deepens compute lock-in, pressures AVGO custom XPU business
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a $3.5B convertible bond investment in MediaTek with an expanded NVLink Fusion partnership spanning AI factories, PCs, and automotive. Multiple analysts view this as NVIDIA playing 'kingmaker' for custom ASIC partners (MediaTek, MRVL) while eroding AVGO's competitive moat in the medium term. NVIDIA CEO Huang stated the Vera Rubin platform generates +$40B of revenue per GW.

bullets.title: AI capex buildout: $11T projected through 2029; $5T debt issuance required in 3 years; NScale closes $3B data center financing
bullets.body: A Dwarkesh podcast cited $11T of AI capex projected through 2029, requiring ~$5T of debt issuance in 3 years (META recently issued at 5-6%). NScale closed ~$3B in investment-grade-rated financing for AI data centers in Texas and Wisconsin. Trump publicly called on communities to embrace data centers, and hyperscaler non-commenced power leases stand at 25.5 GW (+346% YoY). U.S. electricity demand growth is now forecast at 5.7% annually through 2030, up from <1% historically.

bullets.title: JPM tactically favors Mag7 over AI/Semis/Memory; infrastructure still better positioned than application software
bullets.body: JPM's trading desk recommends rotating from AI/Memory/Semis to Mag7 and Software into September. Separately, a market commentator (Keller) argues AI infrastructure (NVDA, MU) offers more attractive exposure than higher-valued application software (CRM, Workday) which faces unresolved AI disruption risk. AIDC demand is running at 2x deliverable supply, and MRVL optics performance is driving estimate raises.

bullets.title: Apple CEO transition: Tim Cook steps down after 15 years; John Ternus (hardware chief) becomes CEO Sept 1; Phil Schiller resigns from App Store role
bullets.body: Tim Cook's 15-year tenure as Apple CEO ended August 31; hardware chief John Ternus succeeds him effective September 1, with Cook becoming executive chairman. Apple's market cap grew from under $350B to nearly $4.7T under Cook (~11.4x, or 17.6% annualized). Phil Schiller also resigned from his App Store and events management roles the same day.

bullets.title: FTC sues Amazon over alleged advertiser price manipulation; AMZN down 2.5%; Amazon disputes all claims
bullets.body: The FTC filed suit against Amazon alleging it deceived advertisers on retail platforms. Amazon's response disputed the lawsuit, claiming CPC for Sponsored Products stayed flat adjusted for inflation from 2019-2024, average winning bids fell 50%, and advertisers saved $8B from 2021-2025 under its relevancy-based model. Piper Sandler reiterated AMZN Overweight at $320, calling it 'best positioned' for AI spending with ~14% ROIC expected in 2026.

bullets.title: HPE Q3 earnings preview (Sept 2): consensus $11.95B revenue, AI/Cloud segment $8.66B; options imply 11.4% move
bullets.body: HPE reports Q3 earnings September 2 after close. FactSet consensus is $11.95B revenue (vs. $11.5-12.1B guidance range) and $0.93 EPS. FY guidance implies 29-33% revenue growth and 80-85% operating income growth. HPE stock is +11.1% since June 1 vs. S&P 500 +1.1%. Options imply ~11.4% post-earnings move; EPS beat rate is 16 of last 20 quarters.

bullets.title: RBLX +7.1% on EU Digital Services Act scrutiny; EU also designates ChatGPT and Reddit as 'Very Large' platforms
bullets.body: EU flagged Roblox for higher Digital Services Act scrutiny, which paradoxically drove RBLX shares up 7.1%. EU also designated ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox as 'Very Large' platforms, imposing additional compliance requirements. Separately, OpenAI's ChatGPT advertising business hit $1B annualized run rate and opened its ads manager for direct purchases in India, Europe, Middle East, and North Africa today.

bullets.title: German CPI misses estimates at 2.9% YoY vs. 3.1% expected; Bessent calls core inflation 'very tame'
bullets.body: Germany's preliminary August harmonized CPI rose 2.9% YoY, below the 3.1% estimate, with M/M at 0.2% vs. 0.3% expected. Bessent separately characterized US core inflation as 'very restrained,' arguing traditional central bank policy does not raise rates into supply shocks—a potential counterweight to hawkish Warsh signals.

bullets.title: CXMT begins small-scale HBM3E production; Samsung locks 70% of capacity in long-term deals through 2031
bullets.body: China's CXMT began producing HBM3E in small quantities for AI processors—removing a key bottleneck for China's domestic AI accelerator ecosystem and shifting the constraint to other components. Separately, Samsung Memory has allocated ~70% of its production capacity under long-term contracts through 2031. SK Hynix clarified it is not considering Intel Foundry for HBM4E base die production, sticking with TSMC.
